messages:
sara-cs: Heads-up — HalcyonPay opened a ticket: they say the model is returning more confident but incorrect assertions after the routing override we deployed at 09:12 UTC (rollout r-2026-03-17-09). They included two examples, pasted below.

HalcyonPay: "Prompt: \u003cRequest: Summarize partnership status between Acme Bank and Northbridge Insurance in 2023\u003e
Model response: 'Acme Bank signed a multi-year strategic distribution agreement with Northbridge Insurance on 2023-04-15; press release available at acme.com/press/nb-2023.'

(We do not have any such partnership and no press release.)"

sara-cs: Customer says this started immediately after the routing override: traffic that used to land on model v3.0 default -> now goes to v3.1-fastpath for lower tail latency. They noticed the issue on ~300 requests over the last 30m; severity: P2.

maria-ml: Can you drop the exact request payloads + request_ids? Also which model id was used (full name/hash) and whether quantization changed. Hypothesis: fastpath variant might be using a different tokenizer or a cached prefix that mismatched context, causing assertive completions.

sara-cs: Pasted one request blob and request_id: 
```
{"request_id":"rq_92b7f4","model":"redwood/v3.1-fastpath","input":"Summarize partnership status between Acme Bank and Northbridge Insurance in 2023"}
```
They also attached the raw user message and the full responder output; I uploaded both to the ticket (TKT-5462).

eli-eng: Can infra share the routing diff for r-2026-03-17-09 and the policy that pins traffic to v3.1-fastpath? If we can repro locally I'll try a quick pin/rollback for HalcyonPay to v3.0 to stop further bad responses.

infra-bot: Rollout r-2026-03-17-09: routing policy changed -> default -> v3.1-fastpath (previous default: v3.0). Change request: deploy/route/6789. Link: https://deploys.redwood.internal/route/6789 (ops runbook: /runbooks/route-rollback).

maria-ml: Repro plan: 1) replay the customer's 50-sample set against v3.0 and v3.1-fastpath with identical tokenization settings. 2) run token-level diff and top-k logprob traces for hallucinated assertions. Please include the exact stop/temperature parameters — sometimes fastpath runs with T=0.0 config differences.

sara-cs: Customer confirms they used default params — no temperature override. They've asked for timeline and mitigation ASAP. I'll request a pin to v3.0 for their org while you run repro.

eli-eng: I'll open a short-lived routing rule to pin HalcyonPay org -> v3.0 and notify CS when done. If rollback stops the behavior we can schedule a controlled canary for the fastpath variant.

maria-ml: If rollback reduces hallucinations, we need to diff the compiled kernels and tokenizer tables between v3.0 and v3.1-fastpath. Also worth adding their prompts to our regression eval set and triggering an automated alert if assertive hallucination rate increases beyond baseline.

sara-cs: Action items: 1) Eli to pin HalcyonPay to v3.0 (in progress). 2) Maria to run the 50-sample repro and share traces (requested). 3) CS to update HalcyonPay with ETA and mitigation. I'll escalate to AM & add to incident tracker if we see the same increase for >5 customers. :eyes:

HalcyonPay: Thanks — appreciate the quick response. We'll keep logs and send any more examples.

eli-eng: Pin applied for org halcyonpay (rollout rollback link: https://deploys.redwood.internal/route/6789/revert). Please verify customer traffic is now routed to v3.0.

maria-ml: Running evals now. If anyone has a short list of other customers who hit the fastpath variant this morning, please add them so we can check for correlated regressions.

sara-cs: Adding this to TKT-5462 and pinging AM. Will follow up in the ticket with customer confirmation once traffic is pinned. :thumbsup:
